look_here_first: Check the thick, often somewhat fleshy narrow alternate leaves and the long terminal cluster of small yellow heads, often borne predominantly on one side of branches. Coastal wet-saline habitat is a supporting cue, not proof by itself.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Rhizomatous perennial goldenrod of coastal marshes, dunes, and brackish margins.; Leaves alternate, comparatively thick and narrow; inspect leaf texture and venation rather than flower color.; Numerous small yellow composite heads in a terminal, often one-sided inflorescence.; Inflorescence architecture and fleshy leaf texture together are more useful than plant height.; Check mature involucres and foliage against closely related seaside goldenrods before final ID.

lookalikes.differences: The seaside-goldenrod complex needs current accepted-name and geographic context; older references may fold S. mexicana into S. sempervirens. Inland S. altissima and S. canadensis typically have thinner serrate, three-nerved leaves and broader arching panicles; S. gigantea also differs in stem surface and inland ecology. Confirm with leaf thickness, venation, heads, and range together.
